components.name: Change equation
components.description: The Holdings focal moment, open on the page like Flow's headline pair: "Net worth change = Markets + Added" as three figures (34px for the change, 24px for the parts, tabular) joined by Text Dim operators, the change's percent beside it in Text Dim. Under it, the start and end in words, the definitions behind a closed `<details>` ("What Markets and Added mean · show", dotted Text Dim underline, the state spelled out rather than a caret), and a note when Markets can't cover every investment account (it names them and says their whole change is in Added). Below 480px the change takes its own line.

components.name: Breakdown sum
components.description: Stat tiles joined by their signs: Cash + Invested − Credit owed − Loans = Net worth, owed amounts shown as positive magnitudes after a minus (Text Dim operators: the sign carries the meaning, so it needs AA), never in Out Red. The Net worth tile carries the Selected edge. Below 480px the tiles become a column sum, key left and value right.

components.name: Account row
components.description: One card, one column header (Value / Change / Gain) and a fixed grid, so every group (Cash, Investments, Credit, Loans) lines up; the group total sits in the Value column. A stale sync is an Attention Amber note beside the account. Investment rows open their positions with a real button ("Show 4 positions" / "Hide positions", `aria-expanded`), never a caret ("Show 3 positions and cash" when it holds uninvested cash). Position rows never get a total: they don't sum to the account gain, but their values do sum to the account's value (uninvested cash is its own "Cash · cash" row). Position tables use fixed figure columns so every account's positions line up. A sold position says "sold" under Shares. - **Owed rows** speak in their own frame: Change reads "up $763.14" / "down $410.00" (what's owed), not the net-worth sign beside an "owed" value, which reads backwards. - **Reasons are visible, never `title`-only.** A missing figure is "—" with an sr-only reason, and the table carries one Text Dim footnote ("— under Unrealized: the broker reports no cost basis"). "from first snapshot" shows only on accounts that started later than the rest; when all did, the hero says it once. - **Range switches keep the old figures** dimmed (`hd-busy`, 0.55 opacity after 150ms, `aria-busy`) until the new ones land; only the newest request may write. "Loading…" (`role=status`) appears only on first load. - Below 720px figures move under the name with their own keys, and each position becomes two lines (holding and value, then labelled shares, gain and unrealized, the basis under the unrealized gain).

narrative.overview:
outflow records observations, not verdicts. The person's own history is the baseline: a charge is "unusual" because it's unusual *for them*, never because it broke a budget. The interface reads like a well-kept notebook opened at a desk in the evening: a dark, calm page, dense rows of dated entries with tabular figures, and an annotation in the margin only where something deserves a second look.

Density is high and type is small, because the main reader sits at a desktop and wants many rows in view. Depth comes from tonal steps between near-black navy surfaces and hairline borders, not from shadows. Colour is an ink used for meaning: money in, money out, the kind of account, and things that need attention. The chrome around the data stays neutral so the figures carry the page.

Controls are tactile and clear. They sit quietly at rest but always look pressable: a visible border, a real hit area, and a distinct pressed and focused state.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, single theme (`color-scheme: dark`); near-black navy page with slightly lifted panels.
System sans-serif throughout; all figures use tabular numerals.
One interactive accent (Field Teal); every other hue encodes data meaning.
Flat: hairline borders and tonal layering, no drop shadows on content.
Narrow reading column (940px max) centred on the page.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Rule
rules.body: Every hue other than Field Teal encodes data meaning (in, out, account kind, attention). Chrome, layout and decoration stay on the neutral ramp. If a colour doesn't answer "what kind of money, or does this need me?", it shouldn't be there.

rules.name: The Not-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: In versus out is never told by green versus red alone. The sign, a label or the lane always carries it as well.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every money figure uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` and right-aligns in columns, so digits line up down the page.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by a 1px Hairline border or a tonal step, never by a shadow.

dos: **Do** use the `--lg-*` custom properties in `app/src/ledger.css` for every new colour; they are the live token set.
**Do** keep money figures tabular and right-aligned.

**Do** give every control a visible border and a pressed and focused state, so it reads as pressable on the dark page. Form fields and small outline buttons use Text Faint for that edge: Hairline is about 1.3:1, and a control's boundary needs 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11).
**Do** put focus somewhere sensible after an action removes the control that had it, and keep an Undo toast up until it's used or dismissed.
**Do** put one Key button per action group, at most.
**Do** mirror token values into constants when SVG presentation attributes can't read CSS variables (as `Holdings.tsx` does), and keep them in sync.
donts: **Don't** use the legacy `theme.css` palette (`--bg`, `--card`, `--accent`, the teal-to-blue gradient) for new work. Only the auth gate, toast and a few fallbacks still read it.
**Don't** add drop shadows to content surfaces.
**Don't** use colour for decoration; see the Meaning-Only Rule.
**Don't** signal in versus out by colour alone.
**Don't** put destructive or upkeep actions on an analysis screen; they belong in Settings.
